question: Will an Atlantic hurricane exist at any point between October 1 and October 3, 2026?

calls.reasoning: As of 2026-09-22 the Atlantic has 6 named storms and 0 hurricanes (NHC season table, ACE 6.3, 92% below normal). Fay peaked at 60 kt and is going post-tropical today; nothing can carry into the window. The only NHC-flagged area is an African wave at 0%/30% (2d/7d) in unfavorable shear, so genesis before ~Sept 29 is largely excluded and any YES needs genesis ~Sept 27-Oct 2 plus a jump to 64 kt inside a 72-hour window. This season has converted 0 of 6 named storms to hurricane; even strong-El-Nino analogs (1997, 2015) converted ~40%, so a regularized conversion rate of ~0.18 applied to ~0.6 expected genesis events in the relevant window gives ~6%. Counterweight: CPC GTHO flags 20-40% genesis areas off Africa and north of the Bahamas for the Sept 30-Oct 6 week, MJO/CAG signals point to relaxing shear at month's end, and Fay went from nothing to 4 kt shy of hurricane in two days - so the surprise-hybrid pathway is live. Polymarket season totals imply ~64% for any hurricane in the remaining season, which top-down suggests ~9% for this window; I discount toward the bottom-up figure because the empty 7-day outlook specifically suppresses the front of October.

calls.reference_class: El Nino Atlantic seasons, 1966-2025: was an NHC-classified hurricane active at any point during Oct 1-3 (1982, 1987, 1991, 1997, 2002, 2006, 2009, 2015, 2023 -> YES in 2002, 2006, 2015)

calls.reasoning: Nothing can carry hurricane status into the window: Fay (season peak 70 mph, ~60 kt) is at 40 mph and post-tropical as of 2026-09-22, and NHC's 7-day outlook through ~Sep 29 lists exactly one area — an African wave at near-0%/48h and 30%/7d in conditions NHC calls not particularly conducive — with no Caribbean, Gulf or western-Atlantic area at all. YES therefore needs genesis ~Sep 27-Oct 1 plus attainment of 64 kt by Oct 3, in a season that has converted 0 of 6 named storms to hurricane under the strongest MDR shear since 1979 and a record-strength El Nino. Pathway decomposition: Cabo Verde wave 0.30 x ~0.12 = 3.5%; unlisted CAG / north-of-Bahamas spin-up needing rapid intensification in the region El Nino suppresses hardest in October = 2%; surprise = 1%. Two independent market cross-checks agree: the season-count book implies ~1.0-1.1 remaining hurricanes, giving ~10-12% for a uniform 3-day October window before discounting for the confirmed-empty front of the month, and the September book implies a ~1.2%/day genesis-to-hurricane hazard, i.e. ~4-6% over Oct 1-3. Upside risk is a Joaquin-2015-style western-Atlantic surprise, which CPC's 20-40% genesis area explicitly allows and Fay's 60 kt peak shows is not far out of reach.
calls.reconciliation: Settled factually from the dossiers: (1) 6 named storms / 0 hurricanes as of Sep 22, superseding the background's 5; (2) Fay peaked at 70 mph (~60-61 kt), below threshold, and is post-tropical today, so no carry-in is possible — Run 1's 60 kt and Runs 2-4's 70 mph are the same fact in different units; (3) the NHC TWO fetched directly (30%/7d, one area) beats Run 4's AccuWeather paraphrase of 'no development expected in 7 days'; (4) Run 2's El Nino base rate of 1-in-8 is wrong — Lili was a Cat 4 on Oct 2, 2002 with an Oct 3 Louisiana landfall, and Isaac was a hurricane Sep 30-Oct 1, 2006 — so the El Nino class rate is ~30% as Runs 3 and 4 had it, a mild upward correction to Run 2's framing; (5) no market contract matches this question's threshold, window or resolution source (the Polymarket brackets key on first-hurricane FORMATION and end Sep 25), so the books are evidence, not an anchor. Could NOT settle without web access: whether a GTHO was issued after Sep 15 and which week its 20-40% areas map onto Oct 1-3 — Run 4 labels the same text ~Sep 22 while Runs 1 and 3 found nothing newer than Sep 15; I let that claim carry its uncertainty, noting it is a genesis probability over a 7-day area, not a hurricane probability, and that the outlook itself places lowest shear in the week AFTER the window. The remaining dispute — how much weight the CAG / north-of-Bahamas pathway deserves — is pure judgment with no evidence breaking the tie; I weight it low, because NHC listing no Caribbean or Gulf area through Sep 29 is more recent and more specific than week-old model chatter. Both bottom-up (~6%) and both market cross-checks (~4-6%) converge, so I land at 0.06 rather than outside the runs' range.

disagreements.verdict: Same fact in different units; NHC peak 70 mph ~= 60-61 kt, below the 64 kt threshold. Immaterial — Fay is post-tropical on Sep 22 and cannot carry into the window.

disagreements.claim: The season has 5 named storms (background) vs 6 (all dossiers, NHC table Sep 22)
disagreements.verdict: 6 — Fay was added Sep 19. Hurricanes remain 0, ACE ~6.3.

disagreements.claim: NHC expects no development in 7 days (Run 4 via AccuWeather) vs one area at 30%/7d (NHC TWO fetched by Runs 1-4)
disagreements.verdict: The directly fetched 0800 EDT Sep 22 TWO wins: one African wave, near 0%/48h, 30%/7d, no Caribbean/Gulf/western-Atlantic area through ~Sep 29.

disagreements.claim: A CPC Global Tropics Hazards Outlook was issued ~Sep 22 (Run 4) vs nothing newer than Sep 15 retrievable (Runs 1, 3)
disagreements.verdict: Unsettled without web access — identical valid period (09/23-10/06) and identical 20-40% areas suggest one product, most likely Sep 15. Material point survives either way: it is a genesis probability, and it places lowest shear in the week after the window.

disagreements.claim: El Nino seasons with a hurricane active Oct 1-3: 1-of-8 ~12% (Run 2) vs ~3-of-10 ~30% (Runs 3, 4)
disagreements.verdict: Run 2 is wrong — 2002 (Lili, Cat 4 Oct 2, landfall Oct 3) and 2006 (Isaac, hurricane Sep 30-Oct 1) both qualify. Class rate ~30%, a mild upward correction; but the class is a loose match since those seasons had already produced hurricanes before October.

disagreements.claim: Some traded contract can anchor this question
disagreements.verdict: No. Polymarket date brackets resolve on FIRST HURRICANE FORMATION and terminate Sep 25; season-count books carry no date constraint; nothing on Kalshi/Manifold covers Oct 1-3. Used as evidence via hazard-rate translation only.

disagreements.claim: How much weight to give the Central American Gyre / north-of-Bahamas pathway
disagreements.verdict: No evidence breaks the tie. I weight it low (~2% of the total) because NHC's Sep 22 outlook lists no Caribbean or Gulf area at all through Sep 29, and El Nino October shear is worst precisely there.

disagreements.claim: How much to discount the market-implied ~10-12% uniform-October window figure
disagreements.verdict: Roughly halve it. The discount is earned by a specific, checkable fact — an empty basin at 9 days' lead covering the front of the month — not by general caution.
